subject: Rick Caraviello City Council Candidacy
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Medford City Council candidate Rick Caraviello regarding his platform, political background, and community service. Caraviello shared his positions on residential zoning, municipal overrides, local economic growth, and the city charter reform.

items.title: Introduction and Call for Candidates
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced the program and extended an open invitation for any local candidates running for office in Medford to appear on the show.

items.title: Candidate Background and Motivation
items.summary: Caraviello shared his background as a lifelong Medford resident and community volunteer, explaining that he is running to help address political division in the city.

items.title: Community Accomplishments
items.summary: Caraviello highlighted his past contributions to the city, including raising funds for the public library, supporting youth hockey, and organizing assistance programs for local veterans.

items.title: Stance on Zoning and Development
items.summary: Caraviello expressed opposition to radical residential zoning changes, advocating instead for protecting single-family neighborhoods and encouraging smart, limited commercial growth in local squares.

items.title: Discussion on Financial Overrides
items.summary: Caraviello stated he did not support the recent $7 million override, arguing that override votes should be reserved for large capital projects rather than operational costs.

items.title: Economic Development and Business Collaboration
items.summary: Caraviello proposed growing the commercial tax base by consulting directly with property and business owners to align municipal development plans with private investment.

items.title: Traffic, Infrastructure, and Curb Appeal
items.summary: Caraviello criticized current traffic calming measures for causing congestion and advocated for road repaving pilots, full-time sidewalk crews, and stricter municipal code enforcement.

items.title: City Council Meeting Schedule
items.summary: Caraviello criticized the council's current bi-weekly schedule for dragging meetings late into the night, promising to propose a return to weekly meetings if elected.

items.title: Revised City Charter
items.summary: Caraviello voiced support for the citizen-driven charter changes but objected to provisions added by the City Council that allow for council staff, expense reimbursements, and raises.

items.title: Personal Activities and Campaign Outreach
items.summary: Caraviello discussed his personal routine of supporting local businesses and provided the schedule for his upcoming campaign fundraiser along with his personal contact details.

items.title: Closing and Station Information
items.summary: Petrella closed the program by thanking the guest and the volunteer production crew, and shared the broadcast schedule and website details for the show.
